decisions.mark: identifies the cancellation observer thread as existing to bridge an atomic into a plain int, because the C ABI boundary cannot carry an atomic
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`entropic_interrupt` is documented thread-safe and works by setting an atomic flag. The C ABI carries only `int*`, so no atomic crosses the `.so` boundary. The poller threads bridge the int to the atomic." | WHY: The answer says the C ABI carries only int*, so the cancel poller threads bridge the atomic to the int, which is the item's mechanism. || QUOTE: "`entropic_interrupt` is documented thread-safe and works by setting an atomic flag. The C ABI carries only `int*`, so no atomic crosses the `.so` boundary. The poller threads bridge the int to the atomic." | WHY: The answer says the C ABI carries only `int*`, so no atomic can cross it, and the cancel poller threads bridge the int to the atomic. || QUOTE: "The C ABI carries only `int*`, so no atomic crosses the `.so` boundary. The poller threads bridge the int to the atomic." | WHY: The answer states the poller threads exist to bridge int and atomic because the C ABI can't carry an atomic, which matches the item, even if it calls them "cancel pollers" rather than "observer."
